Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class Desktop2D

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.Desktop2D
Direct Known Subclasses:
DesktopSwing
public class Desktop2D extends Object
The conventional-Swing desktop used when Java 3D is unavailable: one undecorated, maximised window holding an MDI JDesktopPane over the usual lg3d wallpaper, with the Swing Desktop2DTaskbar along the bottom.

Applications come from the same .lgcfg descriptors the 3D start menu reads (Desktop2DMenuConfig). Those whose user interface is a plain Swing panel are hosted in internal frames (Desktop2DWindow); conventional Swing apps that insist on their own JFrame are launched beside the desktop; external executables are started as child processes; and pure Java 3D applications are offered disabled, since there is no scene to render them into.

Nothing in this package touches Java 3D, so the shell also starts on a JVM where the Java 3D jars are missing entirely.

  • Field Details

    • MODE_PROPERTY

      public static final String MODE_PROPERTY
      Set to true while the 2D desktop is running. Code that offers Java 3D-only features (the control center's Appearance/Desktop panels) reads it to leave those out instead of failing.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • QUICK_LAUNCH_FLAVOR

      public static final DataFlavor QUICK_LAUNCH_FLAVOR
      The drag-and-drop flavour that carries a Desktop2D.QuickLaunchItem from a drag source (the Application Launcher frame) to the 2D taskbar's quick-launch strip (the drop target). It is a same-JVM local-object flavour: the 2D desktop hosts both ends in one JVM (frame apps run via a reflective main on a daemon thread), so the item is passed by reference and never serialised.

    • openAgendaAt

      public void openAgendaAt(LocalDate date)
      Opens (or brings forward) the Agenda app navigated to the week containing date. Invoked when the user double-clicks a day in the taskbar calendar popup; the panel is navigated reflectively through Desktop2DAppRegistry.showDate(javax.swing.JComponent, java.time.LocalDate), so lg3d-core keeps no compile-time dependency on the Agenda panel in lg3d-incubator.

    • openHostedPanel

      public static Desktop2DWindow openHostedPanel(String title, Icon icon, JComponent content)
      Hosts an already-built Swing panel in a new (or existing, brought forward) 2D desktop internal frame at runtime. This is the reusable entry point any application uses to open a secondary window inside the 2D desktop - as an MDI Desktop2DWindow, so it belongs to the desktop (and is captured by the desktop screenshot) instead of becoming a stray top-level OS window beside it.

      Returns null when no 2D desktop is running, so a caller can fall back to another host (the 3D Frame3D or a standalone JFrame); this also keeps it headless- and unit-test-safe.

      Parameters:
      title - the window title (also the taskbar / application name)
      icon - the frame icon, or null for none
      content - the Swing content to host

    • isRunning

      public static boolean isRunning()
      Whether a 2D desktop shell is running in this JVM. The counterpart check for postNotification(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.Notification.Kind) and the notification routing in NotificationService.notify: apps on the Swing desktop post toasts here, everything else falls back to the 3D HUD service.

    • currentWallpaper

      public static Image currentWallpaper()
      The desktop backdrop currently painted by the pane, or null when the shell shows its plain background colour. Exposed for the surfaces that sit beside the desktop pane rather than over it - the taskbar is docked in the content pane's edge, so to fade against the wallpaper it has to paint the strip of backdrop that would lie behind it. Null when the 2D desktop is not running, which leaves those surfaces solid.

    • postNotification

      public static void postNotification(String title, String message, Notification.Kind kind)
      Raises a notification on the running 2D desktop, the notification counterpart of applyDesktopConfig(). This is the application-facing hook: desktop apps (Mail, Instant Messenger, ...) post their incoming-event toasts here, in the same spirit as setWallpaper(URL) and the other static control hooks. A no-op when the 2D desktop is not running (e.g. the standalone 3D desktop or a headless test JVM). Safe to call from any thread; the work is done on the EDT.

    • applyDesktopConfig

      public static void applyDesktopConfig()
      Re-applies DesktopConfig to the running 2D desktop: the Swing UI font defaults, the taskbar docking edge (top/bottom) and the taskbar's own geometry (thickness, icon scale, font, auto-hide), and the surface opacities the DesktopTransparency paint path reads. A no-op when the 2D desktop is not running. Safe to call from any thread; the work is done on the EDT. This is the 2D counterpart of the DesktopConfigChangeEvent the 3D taskbar listens for.

    • setWallpaper

      public static void setWallpaper(URL url)
      Sets the desktop backdrop to the image at url, the 2D counterpart of the BackgroundChangeRequestEvent the 3D scene manager listens for. A no-op when the 2D desktop is not running or url is null. The image loads asynchronously; the pane repaints itself as the observer once the pixels arrive. Safe to call from any thread.

    • setNightTint

      public static void setNightTint(float factor)
      Applies the day/night blend factor (0 = full daylight, 1 = full night) to the 2D night veil - the counterpart of re-tinting the 3D scene lights. A no-op when the 2D desktop is not running. Safe to call from any thread; the repaint is marshalled onto the EDT.

    • setSlideshowEnabled

      public static void setSlideshowEnabled(boolean enabled)
      Turns the wallpaper slideshow on or off on the running 2D desktop and persists the choice. Safe from any thread; when no shell is running the value is still written to DesktopConfig so the next start honours it. Called by the control center's Appearance panel.

    • setSlideshowIntervalSec

      public static void setSlideshowIntervalSec(int seconds)
      Sets and persists the slideshow interval in seconds (clamped by DesktopConfig), restarting the running slideshow's timer. Safe from any thread; a no-op on the live shell when none is running.

    • setSlideshowFolder

      public static void setSlideshowFolder(String folder)
      Sets and persists the slideshow source folder (a directory path, or blank for the bundled wallpapers), rescanning the running slideshow. Safe from any thread; a no-op on the live shell when none is running.

    • applyIconPack

      public static void applyIconPack(String packId, String packDir)
      Selects and persists an icon pack, then re-resolves every live icon surface on the running 2D desktop so the switch is immediate: the start menu, the taskbar quick-launch strip, the open-window buttons and the window frame icons. Safe from any thread; when no shell is running the choice is still written to DesktopConfig so the next start honours it. Called by the control center's Customization panel.
      Parameters:
      packId - the pack id to activate (empty for the default/generated icons)
      packDir - the imported pack's folder/zip path, or empty when using a bundled pack or the default

    • setDoNotDisturb

      public static void setDoNotDisturb(boolean enabled)
      Turns Do Not Disturb on (indefinitely) or off and persists the choice, so the next start honours it. When a 2D shell is running the live state is updated on the EDT (its change listener does the persisting); otherwise the value is written straight to DesktopConfig. Safe from any thread.

    • setDoNotDisturbFor

      public static void setDoNotDisturbFor(long millis)
      Turns Do Not Disturb on for millis from now (indefinitely when millis <= 0) and persists the deadline. Live update on the EDT when a 2D shell is running; otherwise written straight to DesktopConfig. Safe from any thread.

    • doNotDisturbSnapshot

      public static Desktop2D.DoNotDisturbSnapshot doNotDisturbSnapshot()
      The 2D desktop's Do Not Disturb state for the control center. Falls back to the persisted config when no shell is running, so the panel still shows the last-set state in 3D mode or headless. Safe to call from any thread.

    • notificationSnapshot

      public static Desktop2D.NotificationSnapshot notificationSnapshot()
      A snapshot of the 2D desktop's notification log (newest first) plus the unread count. Empty when no shell is running. Safe to call from any thread.

    • markNotificationsRead

      public static void markNotificationsRead()
      Marks every logged notification read (clears the tray badge). A no-op when no 2D shell is running. Safe from any thread; runs on the EDT.

    • clearNotifications

      public static void clearNotifications()
      Empties the notification log. A no-op when no 2D shell is running. Safe from any thread; runs on the EDT.

      Sets the number of workspaces (clamped to WorkspaceModel.MIN_COUNT..WorkspaceModel.MAX_COUNT) and persists it, resizing the live model and re-syncing the pager when a 2D shell is running. Safe from any thread.

    • switchWorkspace

      public static void switchWorkspace(int index)
      Switches the running 2D desktop to the workspace at index (wrapped into range). A no-op when no shell is running. Safe from any thread; runs on the EDT.

    • workspaceSnapshot

      public static Desktop2D.WorkspaceSnapshot workspaceSnapshot()
      The 2D desktop's workspace layout (count, current index and the window count on each) for the control center. When no shell is running, reports the persisted count with zero windows on each, so the panel still renders. Safe to call from any thread.

    • applyShortcuts

      public static void applyShortcuts()
      Rebuilds the running 2D desktop's shortcut table from DesktopConfig and re-registers the key dispatcher, so a control-center change takes effect immediately. A no-op when no shell is running. Safe from any thread; runs on the EDT.

    • shortcutBindings

      public static Map<String,String> shortcutBindings()
      The effective shortcut bindings (action id -> keystroke spec) for the control center: the defaults overlaid by the persisted custom overrides. Empty when no 2D shell is running. Safe to call from any thread.

    • quickLaunchPinned

      public static List<Desktop2D.QuickLaunchItem> quickLaunchPinned()
      The 2D desktop's pinned quick-launch entries, in taskbar order, for the control center. Empty when no 2D shell is running (3D mode or headless), so the panel degrades to an empty list rather than throwing. Safe to call from any thread.

    • quickLaunchCandidates

      public static List<Desktop2D.QuickLaunchItem> quickLaunchCandidates()
      The start-menu applications that can still be pinned to the quick-launch strip - launchable in the 2D desktop and not already pinned - for the control center's "add" list. Empty when no 2D shell is running. Safe to call from any thread.

    • quickLaunchPin

      public static void quickLaunchPin(String command)
      Pins the start-menu application launched by command onto the running 2D desktop's quick-launch strip. A no-op when no shell is running, or the command is blank, is not a known start-menu item, or is already pinned. Safe from any thread; runs on the EDT.

    • quickLaunchUnpin

      public static void quickLaunchUnpin(String command)
      Un-pins the quick-launch entry launched by command from the running 2D desktop's strip. A no-op when no shell is running or it is not pinned. Safe from any thread; runs on the EDT.
